chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Mis'mam said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): I had a female slave who was pregnant, so I vowed to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, that if she gave birth to a boy, I would perform Hajj for him or perform Hajj on his behalf. He (the Imam) said: 'Indeed, a man vowed to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, regarding his son, that if he reached maturity, he would perform Hajj for him or perform Hajj on his behalf. The father died, and the boy reached maturity later. So the boy came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and asked him about that. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered that he be made to perform Hajj on his behalf from what his father had left.'

key_terms.أَحُجَّ عَنْهُ: I would perform Hajj on his behalf
key_terms.أُحِجَّهُ: I would perform Hajj for him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a father vows to perform Hajj for his unborn child and then dies?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the execution of conditional vows (*nadhr*) regarding Hajj, specifically addressing the scenario where the vowor dies before the condition is met. It establishes that the obligation transfers to the beneficiary, who must perform Hajj using the deceased's estate, a ruling derived from the Prophet's directive to the son in the narrated case. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that specific vows are binding on the estate unless explicitly waived, ensuring the fulfillment of the vow's intent.
